supply_situation_summary: British launched offensive with adequate immediate supplies but thin logistical margins. Axis forces operating on extended supply lines but with adequate forward stockpiles.

allied_supply_state.overall_assessment: ADEQUATE - Short-term offensive capability but limited depth

supply_context.strategic_situation: British forces recently rebuilt after Operation Compass. 'Tiger Convoy' (May 1941) delivered 238 tanks and supplies, enabling offensive operations.
supply_context.supply_base: Railhead at Mersa Matruh, Egypt (200km from front)
supply_context.forward_dumps: Sidi Barrani area - 3 days combat supplies forward deployed
supply_context.supply_route: Rail to Mersa Matruh, then truck convoy to forward areas
supply_context.truck_assets: Adequate for 3-day offensive but insufficient for sustained operations

limitations: Long supply haul from Mersa Matruh
Matilda tanks: fuel-hungry (2-3 miles per gallon)
fuel_state.critical_factor: Offensive must succeed quickly before fuel stocks exhausted

tank_main_gun.2pdr_armor_piercing: Adequate stocks - 200 rounds per tank forward
tank_main_gun.note: Critical for tank combat - 2-pdr effective against Panzer III/IV

limitations: High expenditure rates expected in mobile operations

water_state.source: Piped water from Mersa Matruh + trucked supply
water_state.assessment: GOOD - Not a limiting factor for short offensive

issues: Crusader tanks: NEW - mechanical reliability issues, limited spare parts
Matilda tanks: Transmission failures in desert conditions
General shortage of tracks, engines, transmissions
High breakdown rate expected in desert operations
spare_parts_maintenance.impact: Tank losses from mechanical breakdown rivaled combat losses in North Africa

medical_supplies.field_hospitals: Established at Mersa Matruh and Sidi Barrani
medical_supplies.forward_aid_stations: Battalion and regimental aid posts with divisions
medical_supplies.challenge: Heat casualties and tank crew burns (major burden)

axis_supply_state.overall_assessment: MARGINAL - Extended supply lines but adequate forward stockpiles for defensive operations

supply_context.strategic_situation: DAK operating 1,400km from main supply port (Tripoli). Benghazi port partially operational but limited capacity.
supply_context.forward_dumps: Bardia, Sollum, Tobruk perimeter - 5 days combat supplies
supply_context.supply_route: Via Balbia coastal road - 1,400km Tripoli to front
supply_context.truck_assets: Chronic shortage - inadequate for sustained operations
supply_context.vulnerability: RAF interdiction of coastal road + port bombing

fuel_state.assessment: ADEQUATE for defensive operations, MARGINAL for mobile counterattacks
limitations: Panzer divisions: fuel-hungry in mobile operations
British air attacks on supply columns
fuel_state.rommel_factor: Rommel notorious for aggressive operations despite fuel shortages

ammunition_state.assessment: GOOD - Forward stockpiles built up for defensive battle

anti_tank.88mm_flak: Critical importance - adequate stocks at Halfaya Pass
anti_tank.5cm_pak_38: Good stocks but weapon ineffective vs Matilda II

ammunition_state.critical_factor: 88mm FlaK ammunition at Halfaya Pass - carefully rationed for tank kills

desert_context.critical_shortage: Water shortage limited German operational flexibility

issues: Panzer III/IV: transmission and engine failures in desert
Track wear severe on desert terrain
spare_parts_maintenance.german_advantage: Superior field workshop organization vs British

supply_context.strategic_situation: Italian forces supplied through Italian shipping to Tripoli/Benghazi. Separate supply chain from Germans.
supply_context.supply_organization: Italian logistics less efficient than German

limitations: Ariete Division mobile operations constrained by fuel

ammunition_state.note: 47mm tank gun and artillery ammunition sufficient for defensive battle

water_state.note: Italian forces suffered severe water shortages. Many units on reduced rations.

ammunition_reserves_days.advantage: Axis - better forward stockpiling for defensive battle

water_reserves_days.advantage: Allied - shorter supply lines, better water access

maintenance_capability.allied: POOR - new tanks, limited spares, breakdown issues
maintenance_capability.german: GOOD - excellent workshops despite parts shortages
maintenance_capability.italian: VERY POOR - chronic reliability and parts issues

british_offensive_limitations.depth_constraint: Limited ability to exploit success due to supply constraints
british_offensive_limitations.maintenance_crisis: Crusader tank breakdowns reduced effective strength daily
british_offensive_limitations.resupply_challenge: Active combat prevented effective resupply - units fought with initial loads

axis_defensive_advantages.prepared_positions: Forward supply dumps at defensive positions (Halfaya, Capuzzo)
axis_defensive_advantages.shorter_tactical_distances: Defensive operations required less fuel than British offensive
axis_defensive_advantages.ammunition_stockpiles: 88mm FlaK positions well-supplied with anti-tank ammunition
axis_defensive_advantages.maintenance_capability: German recovery and repair teams very effective

historical_outcome.british_exhaustion: By June 17, British forces low on fuel and ammunition, many tanks deadlined
historical_outcome.axis_sustainability: Axis forces able to maintain defensive positions and launch limited counterattacks
historical_outcome.supply_factor: British supply constraints contributed to decision to withdraw

historical_notes.tiger_convoy: HMS Convoy Tiger (May 1941) delivered 238 tanks (including Matildas and Crusaders) plus supplies. This enabled Operation Battleaxe but did not solve underlying logistics issues.
historical_notes.rommel_logistics: Rommel's aggressive operations consistently outran his supply lines. His staff constantly warned of supply crises.
historical_notes.desert_logistics: North Africa became a 'quartermaster's war' - logistics often more important than tactics. Both sides operated at end of 1000+ km supply lines.
historical_notes.italian_weakness: Italian supply organization significantly inferior to British/German. Water and spare parts chronic problems.
historical_notes.aftermath: British supply exhaustion contributed to operational failure. Wavell's inability to sustain offensive led to his relief by Churchill.

sources: British XIII Corps supply estimates from historical records
German DAK supply situation from war diaries and Rommel Papers
Italian supply state from Regia Esercito records
Various operational histories of North Africa campaign
Unit TOE files include supply status fields (schema v3.0+)
data_provenance.note: Detailed supply records often incomplete. Estimates based on historical accounts, war diaries, and comparative analysis.
